result:
Verdict: **reject** (tier1). I wrote `review-verdict.json` at the workspace root.

Summary: the three targeted round-3 fixes (config-file/env-var cgroup override, `+master` force-push stripping, multi-refspec checking) are real and well-tested. But the round's central claim — that the cgroup signal is now unspoofable without root — doesn't hold in this deployment: since worker units run under `systemctl --user` on the same `rajat` account as the interactive shell, that account can just run `systemd-run --user --unit=veridian-worker@x.service ...` to get a *genuinely* matching `INVOCATION_ID` + cgroup with zero spoofing, one command, no special privileges. That fully defeats the guard's core purpose and isn't disclosed or tested. I flagged a secondary, lower-confidence issue too (possible `gh` global-flag-before-subcommand bypass of the merge check) for the same follow-up round to verify. No `.github/workflows/**` files are touched.
